question.leadin: This 18th century ruler issued a decree that created the Smolny [SMOHL-nee] Institute of Noble Maidens, the first public European learning institution for girls.
question.text: Name this Russian empress, whose collaboration with many Enlightenment thinkers earned her the nickname "Enlightened Despot."
question.clue: One hundred wives and daughters of the Greek Infantry Battalion were enlisted to receive this ruler as the "Amazon Company" during a tour of the Tauric provinces.

swap.text: This country was the first to mobilize forces to support Serbia, although it withdrew from the war after a 1917 revolution deposed its king Nicholas II.
swap.clue: Prince Potemkin had a close relationship with its Catherine the Great.

question.text: This leader's policies, including glasnost and perestroika, led to the end of the Soviet Union. He was famously implored by Reagan to tear down the Berlin Wall.
question.clue: Another of his early moves was replacing long-time foreign minister Andrei Gromyko with Eduard Shevardnadze.

swap.text: During the Winter War, Finland named improvised explosives for this Soviet diplomat. He signed the Non-Aggression Pact with the Nazi Joachim von Ribbentropp.
swap.answerHtml: Vyacheslav Molotov [do not accept “Molotov cocktail;” that’s not his name]
swap.clue: This man rejected the Marshall Plan and instigated his own plan, which paved the way for COMECON.

question.text: During his reign, Basil II formed the Varangian Guard out of mercenaries from this state and married his sister to its ruler, Volodymyr the Great. This state based out of a namesake Ukrainian city was destroyed by the Golden Horde.
question.clue: Its leaders used a system of succession in which the throne would pass to the eldest brother of the deceased, called the rota or "ladder" system.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about the Eastern Front of World War II.
swap.text: The Germans' failure to capture this Soviet city on the Volga River was a turning point in World War II. This battle finally ended in early 1943 after Friedrich Paulus' 6th Army surrendered to the Soviets under Georgy Zhukov.
swap.clue: One site of heavy fighting in this battle was Pavlov's House, and forty Soviet soldiers held back hundreds of German tanks and troops for five days hiding in a grain silo.

question.leadin: During this conflict, the Green armies were formed by peasants to prevent other belligerents from requisitioning supplies from their villages.
question.text: Name this conflict in which one side utilized "war communism" to defeat the White Army. That victorious side also briefly allied with and later attacked the Black Army of anarchist Nestor Makhno during this conflict.
question.clue: "War communism" was implemented by the winners of this conflict to ensure supplies for its army.

swap.leadin: This ruler wrote the "April Theses" to justify his leadership of the Bolshevik revolution and probably ordered the death of Tsar Nicholas II.
swap.text: Name this goateed man, the first leader of the USSR.
swap.clue: After the failure of his War Communism policy, he established the New Economic Policy.

question.text: He summoned the first zemski sobor, an assembly of clergy, gentry, and boyars, and he also established a secret police called the oprichniki. For 15 points, name this Rurikid dynasty monarch.
question.answerHtml: Ivan the Terrible [or Ivan IV; or Ivan Grozny; prompt on Ivan]
question.clue: He caused a miscarriage in his stepdaughter by beating her, and also killed his son with a blow to the head.

swap.text: This Soviet general helped lead the counteroffensive against the Japanese army in Manchuria. He won the Battles of Stalingrad and Kursk and later protected Khrushchev from an attempted coup by the Anti-Party Group.
swap.clue: This general assisted a future premier in arresting his rival Lavrentiy Beria.

question.leadin: Name these places in where news has occurred over the past few years.
question.text: Terrorists affiliated with Chechnyan guerilla leader Shamil Basayev were responsible for the 331 deaths at a school in this North Ossetian city in 2004.

swap.text: This was the name for the Russian nobles who took advantage of beleaguered tsars during the period. Before coming to power, Boris Godunov was one of these people.
swap.clue: To undermine the influence of these people, a tsar introduced a system in which collegiate registrars were graded "K-14."

question.leadin: This man served as the second leader of the Russian provincial government after the resignation of Georgy Lvov.
question.text: Name this man who took power in Russia after the February Revolution. He served as the first and only prime minister of the short-lived Russian Republic.
question.clue: A July 1917 operation named for this man was the last Russian offensive in World War One, commanded by Aleksei Brusilov.

swap.leadin: Identify these members of Russia's very, very temporary Provisional Government.
swap.text: The "April Crisis," which brought down the Provisional Government, was sparked by a secret message to the allies from this man, the government's foreign minister and the longtime leader of the Kadet party.
swap.clue: Perhaps the most infamous speech delivered to the Russian Duma saw this man exclaim "stupidity or treason?" in reference to Boris Sturmer and the government in general. This man was the founder and major leader of the Constitutional Democrats, better known as the Kadets.

question.text: This city on the Volga drew Persian merchants to its annual trade fair at Makaryev Monastery. A cathedral in this city is named for Alexander Nevsky, a prince of the medieval republic it partially shares a name with.
question.clue: The third most populous city in Russia, it was renamed Gorki during the Soviet period and can be found at the juncture of the Oka and Volga rivers.

swap.leadin: One of these men who was assassinated was likely Grigory Otrepyev, and another one of these men established his base in Tushino.
swap.text: Name these men, the last of whom was possibly named Sidorka and the first of whom came to power in 1605.
swap.clue: The first of these people was alleged to be a defrocked monk named Grigory Otrepiev by a Mussorgsky opera in which he was the main villain.

question.leadin: Name some things discussed in E. P. Thompson's The Making of the English Working Class, 9.
question.text: The preface mentions the English woman Joanna Southcott, who lef behind a wooden box of prophecies. Some crazy people later claimed the box foretold victory in this November 1854 battle during the Crimean War, known as the "Soldier's Battle." Menshikov's loss at this battle to Lord Raglan paved the way for the siege of Sevastopol.
question.clue: One general in this split his column of forces and passed one portion to FF von Mueller.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about a Russian boyar.
swap.text: This man took power after returning to Russia in 1619 and being given the name "Great Sovereign." He would go on to rule as a patriarch until he was succeeded by his more famous son Michael.
swap.clue: This father of Michael Romanov returned to Russia after the Peace of Deulino in 1619, whereupon he was given the title "Great Sovereign" and assumed power until his death in 1633.

question.text: A reduction in the required period of military service was introduced in 1874 by Dmitry Milyutin, who also organized an 1864 genocide targeting these people. The majority of the Egyptian Mamluks came from this group of oft-fetishized Caucasian Muslims.
question.clue: A dynasty of this ethnic group, which includes the Adyghe ("ah-dih-GAY") and Kabardians, replaced the Mamluk Dynasty's Turkic Bahri dynasty.

swap.leadin: Improbable accounts claim that a British spy hid himself in a pavilion where these two rulers met and became friends in the aftermath of a series of bloody battles including Friedland and Eylau.
swap.text: Name these two rulers, who reaffirmed their alliance a year later at the Congress of Erfurt.
swap.answerHtml: Alexander I AND Napoleon Bonaparte [prompt on partial answers for both, including Bonaparte]
swap.clue: One of these two leaders decided to curb the other's power after hearing that he had arrested the Duke of Enghien from Baden , his wife's home town.
